You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

[HarnessEntry(id='arc_stamp_motif_on_exact_zero_shape_matches', kind='memory', title='ARC: stamp motif on exact zero-shape matches', content="For ARC grids with a sparse colored motif embedded in a noisy 0/background-color field, a task may ask to find every translation where the motif's colored-cell mask lands entirely on zeros, then recolor those zero cells with the motif color. Preserve the original motif and every nonmatching cell. Match the original orientation only; do not rotate or reflect unless demos show otherwise. Ignore motif bounding-box cells that are not colored: the match condition is that all motif cells land on 0, not that the whole bounding box matches a fixed pattern. Overlapping matches should produce the union of their motif cells. Demonstrated with a 3-colored 4x5 mask: two same-orientation placements on zeros were recolored, including overlaps, and output differences exactly equaled the union. Another 6-cell 1 mask in a 0/9 field had three placements; the output was the motif color at all their cells. Previous examples also confirmed no rotated/reflected matches. Use demos to verify target background, motif color, and whether orientation changes are allowed. Practical caution: transcribing a grid with even one omitted cell can hide a valid match and produce an invalid-sized output; verify every row has the stated width before matching and before submission. Confirmed again in task-58fa3f1c: a sparse 8-cell color-5 mask in a noisy 0/9 grid had exactly two translations whose mask cells were all 0; stamp 5 on both, preserve the original motif and all other cells.

Another accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c): on a 29x11 grid with background 6, scattered zero cells, and an 8-shaped L triomino with mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}, the rule was to stamp 8 over every translation whose three mask positions were all originally 0. There were 25 placements; preserve all 6s and unmatched 0s and take the union if placements overlap. This confirms the rule also applies when the nonzero background is 6 and the motif has only three colored cells. Compute matches from the original grid, not incrementally from already-stamped cells.

Additional accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c, 16x18): background 0 with scattered color-3 noise and a 7-cell color-2 stencil. In its 3x4 bounding box, the stencil mask offsets (0-indexed) are {(0,0),(0,2),(0,3),(1,1),(1,3),(2,1),(2,2)}. Search all in-bounds translations in the original input and accept one exactly when all seven mask cells are 0; bbox holes are irrelevant. There were 22 placements, with top-lefts (0,7),(0,9),(0,12),(1,3),(1,10),(1,11),(1,12),(3,1),(3,13),(4,2),(5,8),(7,5),(8,0),(8,1),(9,0),(9,1),(11,5),(12,6),(12,7),(12,8),(12,9),(13,6). Recolor the union of their mask cells to 2, preserving original stencil, color-3 noise, and unmatched zeros. Accepted first submission. Reinforces the same-orientation, original-grid mask match across another nonzero stencil color and a denser/asymmetric mask.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 13x13): background 8, zero target cells, and a 5-cell color-5 stencil with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1)} (a top horizontal bar with a two-cell stem below its center). Search original grid for translations whose five mask cells are all 0, ignoring other cells in the 3x3 bounding box. Four matching top-lefts were (2,1),(2,2),(2,4),(4,3). Recolor the union of those five-cell placements to 5; preserve all other cells and the original stencil. First submission accepted. This directly confirms the same-orientation mask-stamping rule for a 5-cell mask against zero speckles on background 8.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 28x13; background 9, motif color 8): The 9-cell mask offsets were {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(4,1),(5,0)}. Search only same-orientation translations where all mask positions are 0 in the original grid, ignoring bbox holes; recolor the union to 8. Valid top-lefts: (9,11) and (14,0). This test was accepted with no wrong submissions.', path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:09:03.303501+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T12:53:35.805495+00:00', version=8), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_bcca5002_shift_foreground_down_one_row', kind='memory', title='ARC task-bcca5002: shift foreground down one row', content='For ARC task-bcca5002, the entire foreground pattern translates downward by exactly one cell while the grid dimensions and background remain unchanged. The sparse marker pixels lie between a boundary bar and the grid interior on the same columns as that bar. For each marker, draw its marker-color ray from the adjacent boundary bar toward the marker, stopping just before it; recolor the original marker to 4. Also map each marker's column offset within its adjacent bar to the corresponding offset within the opposite bar, and project that opposite-bar cell through the interior to the far boundary using the marker color. Preserve both bars, all cells beyond each marker on its local ray, and all unrelated cells. When the bars occupy different columns, offsets are left-to-right within the bar segments (e.g. offset 0 in top segment maps to offset 0 in bottom segment). This describes both the marker-local rays and the full rays projected from the opposite bar; do not draw only a ray from one arbitrary endpoint.

Accepted demo (12x8): background 0; top bar color 6 at row 0, cols 5–7; bottom bar at row 11, cols 0–2; marker 1 at (2,7). Draw 1 at (1,7), change marker (2,7) to 4, and project the matching offset 2 from the bottom bar upward in col 2, rows 0–10. Preserve bars/background.

Marker recolor is always 4, not input-color+1.

Rotated cases with vertical boundary bars are handled by swapping rows/columns: rays run horizontally, and marker row offsets map between opposite edge segments. A related accepted example: background 5; right-edge color-8 bar in rows 0–4, left-edge bar rows 10–14; sparse 1 markers at (10,5),(12,3),(13,6),(14,4). Local rays go rightward from each marker toward the adjacent left bar; markers become 4. Matching row offsets 0,2,3,4 are projected across the opposite right-side segment (rows 0,2,3,4), leaving row 1 unchanged. Preserve bars and unrelated cells.
